headline_marked: [[Northrop Grumman unveils Raid Hunter]] anti-drone chain gun with 50mm precision-guided ammo
headline: Northrop Grumman unveils Raid Hunter anti-drone chain gun with 50mm precision-guided ammo
summary: Northrop Grumman's new Raid Hunter provides short-range air defense, using 50mm precision-guided ammunition to counter drone swarms and cruise missiles. It aims to fill a critical air defense gap against evolving aerial threats.
details: Northrop Grumman has unveiled Raid Hunter, a new short-range air defense system designed to counter increasingly complex aerial threats. It utilizes the firm's proven Chain Gun technology and precision-guided 50mm ammunition to defend against drone swarms and cruise missiles. This solution aims to fill a critical short-range air defense gap.

Modern air defense systems have struggled with high-volume drone swarms and low-flying cruise missiles, as seen in recent conflicts. Traditional defenses, designed for warplanes, are often overwhelmed or find expensive anti-air missiles disproportionate for cheaper, numerous drones. Raid Hunter addresses this economic and operational challenge.

Central to the Raid Hunter is its large-caliber, high-rate-of-fire Chain Gun, paired with precision-guided 50mm ammunition. This combination is designed to be cost-effective, capable of deep magazines, and allows for fast reloads, making it suitable for engaging massed swarming threats.

The system features a modular, palletized design, enabling rapid deployment on vehicles like the C-130. Multiple Raid Hunter units can operate as an integrated, networked system, allowing for sensor fusion and coordinated engagements. It also integrates with existing layered defense architectures.

Northrop Grumman is continuing tests of the Raid Hunter throughout this year to validate its counter-UAS and air defense capabilities. The goal is to support accelerated fielding of these new air defense systems to address urgent operational needs.

headline_marked: [[PawBot: An AI desktop puppy]] that eats your files and lives in your browser
headline: PawBot: An AI desktop puppy that eats your files and lives in your browser
summary: Inspired by 90s desktop pets, this pixelated golden retriever is powered by Google Gemini, offering mood-aware barks and interactive feeding by dropping files or emoji.
details: PawBot revives the classic desktop pet experience for 2026, featuring an AI-powered pixel golden retriever puppy. This interactive companion lives in your browser, capable of 'eating' files, emojis, or text you drop onto it, and responding with mood-aware barks.

The puppy boasts full sprite animations for various actions like idle, walk, run, eat, and sleep. It reacts to user interaction, chasing dropped items and curling up with sad eyes if ignored for too long, mimicking a real pet's behavior.

Powered by Google Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite, PawBot uses the LLM as a personality engine rather than a chatbot. Users can install it as a Chrome extension by cloning the repo and loading it unpacked, requiring a free API key from Google AI Studio for full functionality.
